Plot saved diagnostics from the selected allocation fit

Source: R/07-allocation_results.R, R/06-ae_methods.R
plot.ae_multistart_fit.Rd

plot() of a fit draws a diagnostic of its selected fit, fit$best, which has the same method. The plots read what the fit saved; nothing is recomputed.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ae_multistart_fit'
plot(x, type = c("fit", "convergence", "state"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'ae_problem_nfxp_fit'
plot(x, type = c("fit", "convergence", "state"), ...)

Arguments

x

An allocation fit from fit_allocation() (an ae_multistart_fit), or its selected fit fit$best.

type

The diagnostic to draw:

  • "fit" (the default): the observed against the fitted values of the fitted output (the facility totals, or every cell of a flow matrix), with the line where they are equal.

  • "convergence": the error of the equilibrium solver at each iteration of the evaluation at the fitted values (a single iteration for the models of clm_allocation() and huff_allocation(), whose state does not depend on the allocation).

  • "state": a histogram of the model state at the fitted values, the attractiveness of the facilities.

...

Graphics arguments passed to graphics::plot() ("fit", "convergence") or graphics::hist() ("state"), such as col, pch or breaks. main, xlab and ylab replace the default title and axis labels.

Value

Invisibly: for "fit" the range of the plotted values, for "convergence" the solver history (a data frame with one row per iteration), for "state" the state at the fitted values.

Examples

# West Cornwall: the small areas and practices west of easting 170 km
areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa)
areas <- areas[!areas$scilly & areas$cent_x < 170000, ]
gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp)
gp <- gp[!gp$scilly & gp$easting < 170000, ]
inputs <- prepare_allocation(stats::setNames(areas$registered, areas$lsoa),
                             stats::setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice),
                             cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice])

# A fit to the registrations of these residents at these practices
flows <- cornwall_flows[cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% areas$lsoa &
                          cornwall_flows$practice %in% gp$practice, ]
totals <- sapply(split(flows$patients, flows$practice), sum)
fit <- fit_allocation(clm_allocation(inputs, fit_v0 = TRUE), totals,
                      loss = "poisson")

# Observed against modeled registrations at each practice, with a title of
# your own
plot(fit)

plot(fit, main = "West Cornwall practices", pch = 19)


# The state of this model is the attractiveness of the practices: their GP
# FTE, since kappa and beta are 1
plot(fit, type = "state", breaks = 10)
